newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia aims to join NATO in first wave.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia aims to join NATO in first wave.

text.p: Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler on Tuesday underlined Slovenia's determination to be among the first wave of countries to join an enlarged NATO.
Thaler said he expected a meeting between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki later this month to ease preparations for NATO's expansion.
"Slovenia is especially interested in the result of this meeting because it expects to be invited to take place in the first round of NATO enlargement," Thaler said in a statement.

Countries of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation are expected at their July summit to invite Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to start negotiations on joining the alliance. Slovenia is believed to be the best placed outsider.
"Slovenia fulfils all conditions (for NATO membership) with a democratic system, a market economy, civilian control of the army and unproblematic relations with neighbouring countries," Thaler said.
He noted that Slovenia had never been a member of the Warsaw Pact alliance of East European countries and had already started to build its defence structure in line with NATO standards.
Slovenia is hoping to gain support for its NATO bid from neighbouring Italy, whose Prime Minister Romano Prodi started his first official visit to Ljubljana on Monday evening.
